aspect: It is required for a passport, in principle
description: Citing the Iranian MFA's Main Office for Consular Services, Landinfo reports that male applicants of conscription age seeking a passport must 'in principle' attach a card showing completion of or exemption from military service, in original and copy.
notes: ANSWERS MIL-001-008. The document chain is now sourced to an IRB Response to Information Request, not inference.

description: Refusing to serve without an exemption can result in not being granted a driver's licence - so the same status that blocks the passport also blocks ordinary domestic mobility.
energy_note: Unable to leave the country, and unable to drive across the city.

description: Men who refuse service without an exemption are ineligible for government jobs and, in the IHRDC's phrasing, 'not hired for high-paying jobs'. The penalty is not a fine; it is a permanent ceiling on earnings.
energy_note: Priced out of your own economy at nineteen.

description: IHRDC notes that failing to serve without an exemption can also result in 'a ban on leaving the country without special permission' - an explicit exit control, separate from simply not being issued a passport.

aspect: The card states WHY you were exempted
description: When an exemption is obtained the holder is issued a card which lists the reason for the exemption. A medical or psychiatric exemption is therefore written on a document used as routine identification.
energy_note: Your diagnosis, printed on your ID, shown to every clerk.

aspect: It is used as an identity document
description: Landinfo, citing Iran's National Organization for Civil Registration, notes that completion or exemption cards count as valid photo ID in an application package for a new shenasnameh. The US reciprocity schedule describes both cards as 'readily available'.
Among the non-health grounds for exemption is being the only son of the family - which means the exemption available to most men is an accident of sibling order.
Men exempted before 1990 may never have been issued a card explaining the reason - so an older applicant asked abroad to evidence his status may have nothing to produce, through no fault of his own.
energy_note: A document that was never issued, demanded thirty years later.

aspect: SCENARIO - the card he cannot show either way
description: Omid's exemption card reads, in Persian, the ground on which he was excused. He needs it for the Canadian file. He also does not want a visa officer reading it. There is no version of the document that says only what he wants it to say.
energy_note: The proof you need is also the disclosure you dread.
